title: Synthetic Bio
tagline: Going full-stack to harness 4.5 billion years of engineering infrastructure
blurb: Scaling the infrastructure we already operate to be full stack and yield novel products.
bullet_points: Genetic Engineering — DNA programming, host organism editing, and exotic organism harnessing

title: Security
bullet_points: Contested spectrum is the default — peer adversaries jam, intercept and geolocate. Legacy comms assume permissive environments that no longer exist.
Detection is lethal — emitting is exposure. Units need to move data without lighting up the spectrum.
Interoperability gaps — joint and partner operations stall when systems cannot talk securely across echelons and allies.
Sensors outpace sensemaking — collection has exploded; the bottleneck is turning raw feeds into decisions at speed.
Standoff is shrinking — operators need persistent awareness without putting people or exquisite assets at risk.
Legacy ISR is exquisite and scarce — high-end national systems are over-subscribed. Tactical units need organic, attritable coverage.

title: Biomanufacturing
tagline: Even manufacturing that leverages biology as its smallest machines requires innovation with its largest
bullet_points: 50 years of stagnation — bioreactors and process equipment are legacy industrial designs, barely changed in decades.
Equipment constrains biology — whole classes of organisms and process regimes are off-limits to today's hardware.
Raised ceiling — limitations in legacy bioreactor designs dramatically limit actualized yields compared to known theoretical limits, leaving headroom to improve output through redesigned hardware.
New hardware unlocks novel processes — altering and adding hardware makes it possible to add highly advantageous steps to the biomanufacturing process.

title: Strain Engineering
tagline: Where every biomanufacturing project must start
blurb: Also known as genetic engineering: DNA programming, host organism editing, and exotic organism harnessing. Most production limitations and failures trace back to the organism itself.
bullet_points: The organism is the biggest bottleneck — most production limitations and failures trace back to the organism itself. Deep expertise in the biomanufacturing process can better inform organism design to optimize for these factors.

Organism optimization should be recursive — doing strain engineering and biomanufacturing prototyping within the same company allows for recursive refinement of the host organism in ways few others can achieve.
Data collection starts at zero — an AI-enabled bio lab needs in-house data on the organisms it engineers and the edited DNA going into them as the first data point in its AI pipelines.

Most organisms are undiscovered or unutilized — the vast majority of microbial organisms in nature have not yet been harnessed for biomanufacturing. Expanding the list of usable organisms dramatically expands possibilities.

title: Molecular Engineering
tagline: The success of any biological product is ultimately determined by its usefulness in the real world
bullet_points: Bench success ≠ field success — molecules optimized for lab benchmarks often underperform in real deployment conditions.
Applications demand tailoring — each use case has its own stability, potency, and formulation requirements.

Target molecule is the first gate — no other part of the biomanufacturing process matters or is worth investing in until customers have de-risked their target molecule and its mechanistic capabilities.

title: Cloud Lab
tagline: Bringing commercial biology offerings into the modern era
blurb: Shifting the paradigm from clunky industrial engagements to digitized infrastructure with real-time control for end customers.
bullet_points: Industrial engagements are clunky — customers hand off a project to a salesperson, often with low specificity around the engagement, and wait weeks for a report with no visibility in between.
Single master engagements kill iteration — biomanufacturing benefits from iterative collaboration between stakeholders and customers, which is almost impossible under fixed, one-time purchase orders.

Buyers are familiar with digital procurement — in most other areas of commerce, buyers can log into a portal, control what they are spending and understand what they are getting. Bio shouldn't be any different.

Increased alignment — with a direct portal to the lab, customers can fully understand the offerings and their real-time data, interact directly with the team on the project, and gain insights when they matter most.

title: Signals & Spectrum
tagline: Novel offensive and defensive solutions across the spectrum
bullet_points: The spectrum is a battlespace — every modern engagement opens in the electromagnetic domain, often decisively.
Attack surface everywhere — proliferated commercial RF, drones and IoT create openings on both sides of the fight.
Defensive posture lags — friendly emissions and infrastructure remain soft targets without purpose-built protection.
